sc: POSTPONED
You've postponed Sam's probation review. Again.
POSTPONED
From the first of January, staff can claim unfair dismissal after six months. Not two years.
POSTPONED
And a probation clause in their contract won't change that.
THE CHANGE
That's the government's own wording.
The qualifying period drops from two years to six months, for dismissals from the first of January.
THE CHANGE
And it counts staff you've already got.
Anyone who started by the first of July this year will already have six months' service.
THE CHANGE
And the cap on compensation for unfair dismissal is being removed too.
THE CHANGE
So that review you keep moving? It really matters now.
3 THINGS
Here's what to do.
STEP 1
One. Put every probation end date in the diary,
with a named owner and a reminder well before month six.
STEP 2
Two. Actually hold the review, and write it down.
What was discussed, what was agreed, and the outcome.
STEP 3
Three. Check what the contract says.
How long probation is, whether it can be extended, and the notice period.
KEY DATES
Dogetlawyer keeps every contract in one place,
with key dates like probation end dates, and a task with a name against each one.
YOUR TURN
Be honest. How many times have you moved a probation review? Comment it.
